answers.rationale: Lead with the Delta nonstop. Its $92 premium over the cheapest connection is modest in light of Maya's repeated willingness to pay materially more for a nonstop when schedule reliability matters, and this week she has an explicit physical-therapy reason to avoid a carry-on transfer. It also comfortably meets the arrival requirement.

Lead with the American two-stop. Maya explicitly permits two comfortable protected connections for this trip when they create meaningful savings, and B is $84 to $206 below the workable one-stop alternatives while arriving before the hotel deadline. Its 96- and 103-minute connections are not tight and it has no overnight.

Lead with the Delta via Salt Lake City itinerary. Maya has repeatedly favored meaningful schedule buffer over a small savings, and here specifically asks for a deliberately longer, unhurried connection. A provides a 2-hour-55-minute layover, remains within the arrival deadline, uses only one connection, and costs just $24 more than the shorter 95-minute one-stop option.

Lead with Exchange Hotel. It has the highest rating, the shortest walk to the lab, and on-site dining. Across the three nights, its $9-per-day breakfast makes its effective cost essentially the same as Harborview's included-breakfast rate, while its substantially shorter walk better matches Maya's recurring preference for lower-friction workday logistics over included breakfast.
